summary: The team has done solid engineering groundwork (clean release pipeline, service principals, written data quality rules, table-driven tests, real volumes from discovery), but the status says green while POS data has never been read from the live source, the history load that FR-10 requires has no design or estimate, and the data model calculates revenue differently from the definition the sponsor signed. Several design gaps (voided sales, Cartwell resends and late files, returns up to 60 days back) will quietly produce wrong numbers unless fixed before the gold build in sprint 4. Re-forecast the plan now: the estimate needs about 35 developer-weeks and the plan has about 28.

contradictions.issue: Revenue is signed as excluding VAT and net of returns; the data model builds it including VAT and before returns. Units are 'net of returns' vs 'sum of quantity sold'.
'Near real-time so store managers can act on the day's trading' vs a daily 05:00 batch.
History is 'all' in requirements, 3 years (~200M lines) in discovery, and absent from architecture, plan, estimate and go-live steps.
Plan needs POS access in week 1; the RAID log knew at week 0 that it takes about 6 weeks.
M1 reported Complete and everything green, while M1's exit criterion (query the POS test instance) is unmet and M3 is behind.
35 developer-weeks assume 3 developers for all 12 weeks; the plan reserves weeks 11–12 for SIT/UAT and one developer is on leave weeks 8–9 (~28 available).
Voided sales are physically deleted at source; silver MERGE handles only inserts and updates.
Cartwell resends files (same name or _v2); ingestion appends and silver online orders append, so resends double or are ignored.
Cartwell files arrive after 06:00 on 9 days a quarter; the job runs at a fixed 05:00.
Returns are attributed to an original sale up to 60 days back, but fact_returns_daily writes only business_date = run_date - 1.
Dev is meant to read the POS test instance, but the firewall request covers only test and prod subnets.
Plan shares the dashboard with store managers after the first refresh; steering agreed to wait one week so finance can check numbers.
silver.customer holds marketing_opt_in, but the marketing extract selects all active customers.
Marketing (an extract consumer), the POS owner/DBA and a support team appear in other documents but not in the stakeholder map.

fail_fast_plan.risk: Voids, price corrections and late returns leave gold wrong for past days.
fail_fast_plan.test: On the static extract (or STLK-TST01), void a 3-day-old transaction, correct a 5-day-old line and add a return for a 30-day-old sale, run the job and compare silver detail with gold totals.
fail_fast_plan.kill_line: Any gold date that does not equal its silver detail means gold must rebuild affected dates (not just run_date - 1) before it is built in sprint 4.

fail_fast_plan.kill_line: If totals double, the correction is ignored, or the day publishes without a warning, switch silver to MERGE/replace-by-day and gate the job on file arrival before sprint 4.

premortem: POS access arrived around week 8, CDC was first run against a live source in SIT, and its problems (deletes, the 3-day retention) surfaced in the last two weeks.
Finance compared the dashboard with the board pack in UAT and revenue was off by VAT and returns; trust was lost before go-live.
The history load was discovered as unplanned work in week 10; year-on-year pages (FR-07, a Must) were empty at launch.
Online revenue was double-counted after a Cartwell _v2 resend, or missing on late-file days, and store managers saw it first.
The plan never had room: 35 developer-weeks in about 28, reported green until week 10.
